casedb.artefact_reset_reason: stored by an earlier version of the parser; re-run to read them with the current one

casedb.compact_index_pending: The content index has not been brought up to date yet -- it is still inside the case record, or still in the older uncompressed layout. That happens when the case is opened, and needs free disk space about the size of the index; compact once it has.
casedb.compact_no_room: Not enough free disk space to compact the case: rewriting a database needs room for a fresh copy of it before the old one is replaced. Nothing was changed.
casedb.evidence_removed_note: The exhibit and everything recorded against it were deleted from the case. The evidence file itself is untouched.
casedb.index_converted: The content index was rewritten with its text compressed. Every document is still in it and searches find the same things; it is derived from the evidence and can be deleted and rebuilt at any time.
casedb.index_relocate_deferred: The content index was not brought up to date: the disk does not have room for the new copy. It stays as it is, fully usable, and this is tried again the next time the case is opened.
casedb.index_relocate_failed: Bringing the content index up to date failed, and the new copy was discarded. The index is unchanged and still usable; this is tried again the next time the case is opened.
casedb.index_relocated: The content index moved out of the case record and into the cache folder beside it. It is derived from the evidence and can be deleted and rebuilt at any time.
casedb.index_reset_reason: content index schema updated to record media offsets, region kind and which exhibit each hit came from; rebuild required
casedb.not_a_case: %s is not a Strata case, so it was left untouched. A case is a folder holding case.sqlite; choose that folder, or start a new case.
casedb.note_too_long: A note can be at most %d characters. Split it into more than one note.

logical.note: Logical evidence: files that were handed over, not a copy of media. logfile.page_size: The restart area gives a system page size of %d and a log page size of %d; Strata reads 4096-byte pages, so what follows may be misread.
logfile.data_offset_default: The restart area's page data offset is not one Strata accepts; 0x40 is used.
logfile.restarts_differ: The two restart pages record different current LSNs; the one with the higher LSN is shown as the newest.
logfile.not_clean: The newest restart area says NTFS did not shut down cleanly (or the log was in use when the image was taken).
logfile.torn_pages: %d log page(s) failed their update sequence check and were skipped.
logfile.unrecognised_pages: %d log page(s) held neither log records nor unused space and were skipped.
logfile.truncated: More than %d records were found; the rest are not listed.
